Bishop voted against the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (2017), which reduced corporate taxes from 35% to 21%, citing concerns it would balloon the deficit by $1.5 trillion. He opposed making Bush tax cuts permanent and retaining capital gains reductions for the wealthy. He supported closing offshore business tax loopholes. His NTU score of 22% reflects consistent opposition to tax cuts for upper-income earners and corporations.

Bishop voted with President Biden 100% of the time in 2022 (per FiveThirtyEight), which included major Ukraine supplemental aid packages. As a senior House Appropriations Committee member, he has been in the institutional mainstream supporting continued military and economic aid to Ukraine. He has not called for reduced aid or withdrawal from the conflict.

Bishop opposed photo ID requirements stating they suppress the vote, and supports automatic voter registration, same-day registration, and election-day holidays to expand access. His record consistently favors expanding early voting and making mail-in voting more broadly accessible without requiring an excuse.
